p: Hyperyield is an automated liquidity position management service for HyperEVM. It's designed to be a set-and-forget system that will earn yield from Uniswap V3 style (concentrated liquidity) pools without any intervention on your part.
Hyperyield was designed to be extremely easy to use. Getting up and running takes only a few steps.
Site URL: https://www.hyperyield.cash/
First, you need an account. Click the login button to create an account or log in to an existing one.
Please note: if you log in with your wallet, you will still be provisioned a Hyperyield managed wallet. You cannot use your own wallet with Hyperyield.
Next, you will need to deposit some funds to your Hyperyield wallet. Click the deposit button and follow the steps.
You must deposit either HYPE or WHYPE to your Hyperyield wallet! If you deposit something else, it may not be used in your position.
The deposit modal suggests an amount of 10 HYPE. This is not a requirement, you can deposit however much you want.
Once your deposit is received, browse the available pools and select the pool you want to enter.
You have the ability to adjust the price width for the position you want to enter.

The price width is defined as a percent difference away from the current mid-price of the pool. For example, if the price of the WHYPE/USD₮0 pool is $50, and you choose a 1% price spread, that means your position range will be roughly $49.50 - $50.50.
Click Create position... and that's it! You are now earning yield from the pool.
Hyperyield uses Privy as its wallet provider. All users that log into Hyperyield are provisioned a wallet. Due to how Hyperyield works, users must use this managed wallet and not their own.

Before entering a position, Hyperyield will add itself as a signer to the wallet the user is provisioned. This is necessary for Hyperyield to be able to manage their position on their behalf. Hyperyield uses policies in Privy to restrict what actions it can take with the user's wallet so that it can only interact with the exchange pools and LiquidSwap, our swap provider.
In order to make Hyperyield as simple as possible, it handles all token swapping on the user's behalf. This includes:
Automatically wrapping HYPE to WHYPE
Swapping WHYPE to the two tokens in a pool and vice versa
Swapping from one pool token to the other when rebalancing
Automatically unwrapping WHYPE in order to maintain a minimum balance for gas
Swapping to feUSD for deposits into Felix stability pools
This means that the user only ever has to worry about depositing HYPE into their Hyperyield account.
Hyperyield's backend constantly monitors all open positions to check and see if they are still in range. This check occurs roughly once per minute. If the position falls out of range, it will:
Close the existing position and mark it as "rebalanced". This collects all fees and all collateral in the position.

Check the wallet's current HYPE balance. If it is below the threshold reserved for gas (currently 0.1 HYPE), it will automatically swap an available token back to HYPE (up to 0.2 HYPE). If it's above the upper gas threshold of 0.2 HYPE, it will auto-wrap the excess HYPE to WHYPE and then swap the WHYPE to the first token in the pool.

Calculate, based on the user's current token balances, how much is required of each token to re-enter the pool and perform the swap from one pool token to the other. Please note that sometimes there will be leftover collateral due to pool tick spacing and price movement that can happen during the rebalance procedure.
Re-enter the pool with the maximum amount of capital possible.
A user can always manually close a position at any time. Doing so will tell Hyperyield to perform the following steps:
Close the position and claim all collateral and fees accrued. This marks the position as "closed".
Swap the full token balances for each token received back from the closed position to WHYPE.

Hyperyield offers the ability to take additional actions with the yield generated once a position is rebalanced or closed. By default, Hyperyield will reinvest all earned yield into the next position. However, you can change this strategy on your Account page.
At this point in time, the only other supported yield strategy is depositing into Felix stability pools. When a position is closed, Hyperyield will:
Swap all earned yield to feUSD.
Deposit the feUSD into the stability pool of your choice.

You can view your stability pool balance on your Account page at any time. You can also withdraw from the stability pool. When doing so, you will receive feUSD back in your Hyperyield account along with any other assets earned from the stability pool.

In order to maintain the service, Hyperyield charges a 10% performance fee. This is only charged on the yield that is collected. This gives you the freedom to use as tight of a range as you want without having to worry about swap fees (minus the usual fees charged by the DEX pools).
Fees are charged only when collecting yield from a pool. This occurs:
When manually closing a position with accrued yield.
When Hyperyield rebalances a position due to it falling out of range.

l: How do I modify my position size?
p: Currently Hyperyield does not support adding to or removing liquidity from an open position.

If you want to increase your position size you can deposit more HYPE to your Hyperyield wallet at any time and wait for a rebalance (it will automatically be included then) or manually close and reopen your position.
If you want to decrease your position size you will have to close your position and withdraw the funds to another wallet before re-opening a position.
Users can withdraw funds at any time from Hyperyield.
Be careful withdrawing HYPE if you have an open position. Doing so may cause your account to have insufficient funds for gas and Hyperyield will be unable to manage your position for you.
To withdraw funds:
Click the wallet dropdown and go to Account.
Next to the asset you want to withdraw, click the Withdraw button.
Enter the recipient address and how much you want to withdraw.
Click the Withdraw button and your funds will be sent immediately.

l: How do I export my private key?
p: Because Hyperyield is a self-custodial solution you can always export your private key into a wallet of your choice. Hyperyield never sees your private key at any point in time.

That said, keep in mind that Hyperyield, by necessity, is an additional signer on your provisioned wallet and can perform actions limited in scope to what is necessary to manage a liquidity position. It is strongly discouraged for users to use their Hyperyield wallet for anything outside of normal Hyperyield operations.
If you want to export your private key:
Click the wallet dropdown and go to Account.
Click the Export private key button and follow the instructions.

l: Why does Hyperyield only allow 1 position at a time?
p: For now, this significantly simplifies the service so we only have to consider the entire wallet balance on every rebalance. We plan to allow multiple pools and let you to customize the amount of funds to allocate to each in the future.
Hyperyield offers a referral system that allows you to earn yield generated by everyone you refer.

When someone signs up for Hyperyield using your referral link, you will receive 2% of all yield they generate in perpetuity. This comes out of Hyperyield's performance fee and does not adversely affect the referred user.

You will receive payments on every rebalance or position close in the currencies that they are liquidity providers for. For example, if someone is an LP for UPUMP/WHYPE, you will receive payouts in both UPUMP and WHYPE.
By default, your referral fee wallet is your Hyperyield wallet. We strongly encourage you to set this to another wallet you control.
Referrals can only be set on an account that is less than 24 hours old.
Below is a list of potential future features. It is not an exhaustive list or in any particular order and it may change at any time.
Allow multiple open positions and the ability to allocate a portion of funds to each.
Different position and rebalance strategies.
Include full transaction logs that can be viewed on Hyperyield (you can still view these in your favorite block explorer).
Notification of rebalances via Telegram.
Additional yield strategies.
